tamil: மயிலின் மேல் சுவாமி ஏறிக்கொண்டிருத்தல் முதலியவற்றிற்குக் காரணம் என்னவென்றால்: பிண்டாண்டமாகிய இந்தத் தேகத்திலும் அண்டத்திலும், மூலாஞ்ஞான காரணமாயுள்ள கேவலமாகிய பிரகிருதிமாயையின் அசுத்த கேவலமாகிய அசுத்தாசுத்த மகாஅகங்காரமென்னும் இராக்ஷச அம்சமான சூரதத்துவம் அதின் சோதரமான மூவகைத் தத்துவத்தோடு, அஞ்ஞான தசையில், ஆன்ம அறிவையும், பிண்ட விளக்கமான தேவர்களையும், விஷய விளக்கமான இந்திரியங்களையும், நாடி விளக்கமான யந்திரங்களையும், பிராண விளக்கமாகிய உயிரையும் விழுங்கித் தன்னரசு செலுத்தும். அந்தச் சூரதத்துவத்தை வதைக்கும்போது, மேற்படி தத்துவம் மகாமாயையாகிய மாமரமாயும், மாச்சரியமாகிய கோழியாயும், விசித்திரமாயையென்னும் மயிலாயும், மகா மதமாகிய யானைமுகமாயும், அதிகுரோதமாகிய சிங்கமுகமாயும் விளங்கும். சர்வ தத்துவங்களையும் தன்வசமாக்கி, அகங்காரக்கொடி கட்டி, அஞ்ஞான நாடகம் செய்த தத்துவ அகங்கரிப்பை அடக்கி, பதிபசுபாசம் அநாதி நித்தியம் என்னும் சித்தாந்தத்தை விளக்கிக் காட்டுவதற்காக, மாச்சரிய குக்குடத்தைப் போதமாகிய கையால் அடக்கியும், விசித்திரமாயையாகிய மயிலைக் கீழ்ப்படுத்தி மேலிருந்தடக்கியும், ஆபாசதத்துவங்களைச் சம்மரித்தும், சுத்தவிஷய புவனமாகிய தேவ லோகத்தை நிலைபெறச் செய்தும், இந்திரபதியான ரூபேந்திரனுடைய பெண்ணாகிய தாந்தரதத்துவ மென்னுந் தெய்வயானையை இடப்பாலமைத்தும், இந்திரியங்களாகிய வேடர்களின் கண்ணிற் புலப்பட்ட மானசமென்னும் மானினது கர்ப்பத்திலுண்டான வள்ளியாகிய சுத்த மனதை வலத்தில் வைத்தும், நவதத்துவ காரணமாகிய நவவைராக தத்துவமாகிய வீரர்களைச் சமீபத்திலிருத்தியும், சகல கேவலங்களுக்கும் நினைப்பு மறப்புக்கும் இடையில் விவேகவடிவாயும், பாதம் முதல் நாபி வரையில் உஷ்ணவுருவாயும், நாபி முதல் கண்டம் வரையில் ஆதாரநாடியுருவாயும், கண்ட முதல் புருவமத்தி வரையில் மணியுருவாயும், உச்சியில் ஒளியுருவாயும், புத்தியில் சுத்த அறிவாயும், அனுபவத்தில் நித்தியமாயும், எங்கும் நிறைவாயும், கோணத்தில் ஆறாயும், எக்காலமும் மதங்களில் ஆறாயும், சமயத்தில் ஆறாயும், ஜாதியில் ஆறின் கூட்டமாயும் விளங்குகின்ற உண்மைக் கடவுளே சுப்பிரமணியம்.
translation: Why is the Lord mounted on the peacock, and so on? In this body, the small world (piṇḍa), and in the great world (aṇḍa), there is the Sura tattva, a demonic (rākṣasa) part. It is the great ahankara (the sense of "I"), impure within the impure: the impure kevala of prakriti-maya, which is itself kevala (the state of darkness) and the cause of root ignorance. In the state of ignorance, together with its brothers, the tattvas of three kinds, it swallows the soul's knowledge, the devas who are the shining of the body, the senses that are the shining of objects, the yantras (mechanisms) that are the shining of the nadis, and life, the shining of the prana; and it rules as its own king. When that Sura tattva is slain, the said tattva appears as the mango tree, which is great maya; as the cock, which is envy; as the peacock, which is wondrous maya; as the elephant face, which is great arrogance; and as the lion face, which is extreme anger.

That pride of the tattvas had brought all the tattvas under its power, raised the banner of ahankara and staged the drama of ignorance. To subdue it, and to make plain the Siddhanta teaching that the Lord, the soul and bondage (pati, pasu, pāsam) are beginningless and eternal, He holds down the cock of envy with the hand of awareness. He sets the peacock of wondrous maya beneath Him and holds it down from above. He destroys the false tattvas. He makes firm the world of the devas, the realm of pure objects. He places at His left Deivayanai, the tattva of restraint, daughter of Rupendra, lord of the Indra state. He places at His right Valli, the pure mind, born from the womb of the deer, the mind (mānasam), seen by the eyes of the hunters, the senses. He keeps near Him the warriors, the nine tattvas of dispassion, which are the cause of the nine tattvas. He shines as the form of discernment between all the sakala and kevala states, and between remembering and forgetting; as the form of heat from the feet to the navel; as the form of the adhara nadi from the navel to the throat; as the form of the gem from the throat to the middle of the brows; as the form of light at the crown; as pure knowledge in the intellect; as the eternal in experience; as fullness everywhere; as six in angles; as six among the creeds at all times; as six in religion; and as the assembly of six in caste. This true God is Subramaniyam.
commentary: The war of Murugan against the demon Sura is read inwardly. Sura is the great ahankara, born of root ignorance. With its brothers it swallows the soul's knowledge, the senses and life itself, and rules the body as its own kingdom. Struck down, it takes the forms the story tells: illusion (the mango tree), envy (the cock), wondrous illusion (the peacock), arrogance (the elephant face), rage (the lion face). The Lord does not destroy the cock and the peacock; He holds them under, envy in His hand and illusion beneath Him. His consorts are restraint (Deivayanai) and the pure mind (Valli, born of a deer, mān, a play on mānasam, mind). The sixes of creed, religion and caste are counts of his day; the text does not name them. All of it points to one true God, shining in the seeker as discernment, warmth, light and knowledge.

sections.title: One, Three, Four and Six Faces

tamil: சுப்பிரமணியம் ஒருமுகம், மூன்றுமுகம், நான்குமுகம், ஆறுமுகம் ஆனதற்குக் காரணம்: ஒன்று மிரண்டு மில்லாத ஒப்பற்ற பரப்பிரமசொரூபம் நம் பொருட்டுக் குமூஉக்குறியாய், பாவனைக்கு ஒன்றென்று நிச்சயிக்கும், பரகாரண நிமித்தம் (?) ஆகிய அறிவுருவமே ஒருமுகமென்று ஞானிகள் சொல்லுவார்கள். சுத்தராஜசம், சுத்ததாமசம், சுத்தசாத்விகமாகிய மூன்று குணங்களின் கூட்ட விளக்கமாகிய முக்குண விளக்கமே மூன்றுமுகம். பசுமனம், சுத்தமனம், உள்மனம், சங்கலிதமனம் என்னும் நான்கு தத்துவங்களின் கூட்டவிளக்கமே நான்கு முகம். சத்த அறிவின் மூலம், ஒளி யறிவின் மூலம், சுவை யறிவின் மூலம், பரிசவறிவின் மூலம், வாசனை யறிவின் மூலம், ஆத்ம அறிவின் மூலம் என்னும் ஆறு தத்துவங்களின் கூட்டறிவின் மூலகாரணப் பிரகாச விளக்கமே ஆறுமுகம்.
translation: Why is Subramaniyam shown with one face, three faces, four faces and six faces? The Supreme Brahman, in its own form, is beyond compare and is neither one nor two. For our sake, as a sign, it is fixed as "one" for contemplation; the form of knowledge that does this, the supreme causal occasion [?], is the one face, say the wise (jñānis). The three faces are the shining of the three gunas (qualities) together: pure rajas, pure tamas and pure sattva. The four faces are the shining together of four tattvas: the bound mind (pasu manam, the mind of the soul in bondage), the pure mind, the inner mind and the gathered mind. The six faces are the shining of the light that is the root cause of the combined knowledge of six tattvas: the root of the knowledge of sound, the root of the knowledge of light, the root of the knowledge of taste, the root of the knowledge of touch, the root of the knowledge of smell, and the root of the knowledge of the soul.
commentary: Murugan is imaged with one, three, four or six faces; each count is a stage of knowing. The one face is the knowledge by which the Supreme, beyond one and two, is held as one for our contemplation. The editors marked "supreme causal occasion" with a query [?]: the printed text is uncertain there. The three faces are the three qualities in their purified state. The four are four kinds of mind, from the mind bound in bondage to the gathered mind. The six are the root of the five senses' knowing and of the soul's own knowing.

tamil: மயிலின் காலின்கீழும் வாயிலும் பாம்பு இருப்பதென்ன? விசித்திரமாயையின் காரியவுருவான அகங்காரம் தோன்றி வெளிப்படுங்கால், மூலாங்காரத்திலும் அதிகரிப்பிலும் பிராணவாயு வென்னும் பாம்பானது கீழும் மேலும் உண்டாயினும் அகங்காரத்தின் முகப்பாகிய மயில் வாய் மூலமாய்ப் பிராணவாயுவினது வேகத்தை விழுங்கிக் கொண்டிருப்பது இயற்கைதான்.
translation: Why is there a snake beneath the peacock's foot and in its mouth? When ahankara, the effect-form of wondrous maya, arises and comes forth, the snake, which is the vital breath (prana vayu), arises below and above, in root ahankara and in its increase. Even so, it is natural that the peacock, the face of ahankara, keeps swallowing the force of the vital breath through its mouth.
commentary: In the images, the peacock grips a snake under its foot and in its beak. The snake is the vital breath, stirred below and above whenever the sense of "I" rises. The peacock, the face of that ego, swallows its force. The text calls this natural: the rising ego draws the force of the breath into itself.

tamil: படைவீடென்ப தென்ன? அடங்கி இருக்குமிடம். அடங்கியிருக்கும் ஸ்தானங்களே இயற்கைவிளக்கம் தங்குமிடங்களாகும். இவற்றிற்கு ஊர் ஆறாவானேன்? ஏரகமென்பது அழகு பொருந்திய உள்ளமென்னும் இடம். திருவாவினன்குடி யென்பது திரு-ஆ-இன்ன-குடி: திரு - இலக்குமியாகிய சந்தோஷமும், ஆ-பசுவாகிய விளக்க மென்னுஞ் சீவனும், இனன் - சூரியனாகிய புத்தியும், ஒன்று கூடி விளங்கும் ஆன்மஅறிவின் சுத்தகாரிய இடம். பழமுதிர்ச்சோலை யென்பது இந்திரிய கரண சீவ முதலிய அனுபவப் பழங்களாகிய பிரயோசன வின்பங்கள் நீங்கிக் குறைவற்ற அறிவாய் விளங்கும் இடம். திருச்சீரலைவாய், திருச்செந்தில், செயந்திபுரம் என்பன: சுத்தமனத்தின் முகத்தில் விஷயக் கடலின் அவாவாகிய அலையடித்துக் கொண்டிருக்கும் இடமாகிய கரை, செந்துக்களினது இருதய ஸ்தானமாகிய மனம், அஞ்ஞான சூரனை நிவர்த்தித்துச் சந்தோஷகரத்தைப் பெற்ற பதிமனத்தின் விளக்கம். திருப்பரங்குன்ற மென்பது அசைவிலாத ஒன்றான விளக்கத்தையுடைய விவேக உல்லாச வின்ப நிறைவு. குன்று தோறாடல் என்பது மலைதோறாடல். மலை என்பது அலைவில்லாத உணர்ச்சிக்கு முதற்காரணமா யுள்ள துரிய நன்னிலை. இத்துரியம் பரதுரியம், சுத்ததுரியம், குருதுரியம், சிவதுரியம், சத்திதுரியம் முதலிய துரியமலைகள் அனுபவக் காட்சியில் அனந்தம் உண்டு. மேற் குறித்த அனுபவக் காட்சிகளுக்குத் தேகத்தி லிடம் எவை? கோசத்தினடி, தொப்புளின் கீழ், தொப்புள், வயிற்றில் தொப்புளுக்கு மேல் மார்புக்குக் கீழ், மார்பு, நெஞ்சு ஆக 6.
translation: What is a padai veedu (camp)? A place of abiding in stillness. The places of stillness are where the natural light dwells. Why are their towns six? Erakam is the place called the heart, full of beauty. Tiruvavinankudi is Tiru-Ā-Inna-Kudi: the pure place of action of the soul's knowledge, where Tiru, Lakshmi, that is joy; Ā, the cow (pasu), that is the living soul called shining; and Inan, the sun, that is the intellect, come together and shine. Pazhamudircholai is the place where the pleasures of gain, the fruits of the experience of the senses, the inner faculties, the living soul and the rest, fall away, and one shines as knowledge without lack. Tirucheeralaivai, Tiruchendil and Jayantipuram are: the shore, where the waves of desire from the sea of objects keep beating on the face of the pure mind; the mind, the heart-place of living creatures (jantu); and the shining of the Lord-mind (pati manam), which destroyed the Sura of ignorance and gained the hand of joy. Tirupparankundram is the full joy of exultant discernment, whose shining is one and unmoving. Kunruthoradal is "dancing on every hill". The hill is the good state of turiya (the fourth state, beyond waking, dream and deep sleep), the first cause of awareness that does not waver. Of this turiya there are endless turiya hills in the vision of experience: supreme turiya, pure turiya, guru turiya, Siva turiya, Sakti turiya and others. What are the places in the body for these visions of experience? The base of the kōsam (the genital sac), below the navel, the navel, the belly above the navel and below the chest, the chest, and the heart: six in all.
commentary: Murugan's six great shrines, the padai veedu, are read as six places within where the soul rests. Erakam (Swamimalai) is the heart. Tiruvavinankudi (Palani) is split into syllables: joy, the soul (ā, the cow, pasu, also the bound soul) and the intellect meet in it. Pazhamudircholai ("where ripe fruit falls") is knowledge left when the fruits of pleasure fall away. Tiruchendur's three names give three meanings: the shore where desire breaks on the mind (alaivāy, wave-mouth), the heart of creatures (jantu, heard in Chendil), and victory over ignorance (jaya, in Jayantipuram). Tirupparankundram is steady joy in discernment. "Every hill" is turiya in its countless kinds. The six places in the body rise from the base of the trunk to the heart.

tamil: பிரமாவைச் சிறையில் வைத்த தென்பது யாது? சுத்த மன சங்கல்ப சிருஷ்டித் தொழிலையுடைய பிரமாவாகிய மனத்தைக் கிரியையில் பிரவேசிக்க வொட்டாமல், சுத்த விளக்க விவேக நிறைவாயுள்ள சுப்பிரமணிய தத்துவத்தால் சர்வ பிண்ட விஷயங்களாகிய தோன்றல், வளர்தல், குற்றம் நீங்கல், ஒன்றினிடத்தில் மலைவடைதல், தெளிதல் முதலிய பஞ்ச கிருத்தியங்களை விவேக முன்னிலையில் நடத்துங்கால் சலிப்பறப் பந்தித்து இருப்பதே சிறையிட்டது.
translation: What is meant by putting Brahma in prison? Brahma is the mind, whose work is creation by the resolve of the pure mind. The Subramaniya tattva, the fullness of discernment of pure shining, does not let that mind enter into action. It carries out, in the presence of discernment, the five functions that are the matters of every body: arising, growing, the removal of fault, being bewildered over a thing, and becoming clear. While it does so, it holds that mind bound without wavering. That is the imprisonment.
commentary: In the story, the child Murugan imprisoned Brahma, the creator, for not knowing the meaning of Om. Here Brahma is the mind that creates by its own resolve. Discernment holds that mind still and does not let it rush into action, while the five functions of the inner life go on under its eye: arising, growth, the removal of fault, bewilderment and clearing. They mirror the five divine acts of Saiva teaching: creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace.

tamil: ஈசுவரனுக்கு உபதேசித்த தென்ன? உருத்திர தத்துவமாகிய பிரேரக நிலையான காரண தத்துவ முடிவான ஈசுவர தத்துவத்தினியற்கை ஞானம் ஏறிக் கிரியை குறைந்திருப்பதால், கிரியாகாரண பூதமாயும் ஞானகாரண அமிசமாயும் விளங்கும் பிரணவமாகிய உண்மை நிறைவான கிரியையற்ற நிர்விஷய அனுபவம் ஈசுவர தத்துவத்திற்கு - நியதி செய்வது? - சுத்த விவேக தத்துவ அதிஷ்டாதாவான சுப்பிரமணியம் அன்றித் தோன்றாது. இதுபற்றி யுபதேசஞ் செய்தாரென லாயிற்று.
translation: What did he teach to Isvara? The Isvara tattva is the end of the causal tattvas, the impelling state that is the Rudra tattva. By its nature, knowledge has risen in it and action has lessened. The pranava (the syllable Om) shines as the elemental cause of action and as a portion of the cause of knowledge; it is the true fullness, the objectless experience without action. To the Isvara tattva (that which ordains it [?]) this does not appear except through Subramaniyam, the presiding power of the tattva of pure discernment. For this reason it is said that he gave the teaching.
commentary: The story tells that Murugan taught his father Siva the meaning of Om, at Swamimalai. Here Isvara is a tattva: a level where knowledge has risen and action has lessened. The pranava is the objectless experience, free of action, that is the cause of both action and knowledge. It reaches that level only through pure discernment, whose presiding power is Subramaniyam; so it is said that he taught. The editors queried the words "that which ordains" [?]: the printed text is uncertain there.

tamil: கங்கையிலுள்ள நாணற்காட்டிற் பிறந்தது என்பது என்ன? ஆன்ம இயற்கைக் குணமாகிய தயவே கங்கை. ஆன்மாவின் அனுபவ மத்திய நிலையாகிய சகித்த லென்னும் - சர்வ விஷயங்களிலும் அகங்கார மென்னும் தலையெடாமல் - கீழ்ப்படிந்த குணமே நாணல். இவ்விரண்டின் மத்தியில், அனுபவத்திற்கு இயற்கை விளக்கமாய் விளங்கும் பகுத்தறிவாகிய விவேகம் தோன்றுவதே உற்பத்தியானது.
translation: What is meant by his birth in the reed forest in the Ganga? Compassion (tayavu), the natural quality of the soul, is the Ganga. The reed is the yielding quality called forbearance, the middle state of the soul's experience, in which the head called ahankara is not raised in any matter. Between these two, discernment, the knowledge that distinguishes, arises, shining as the natural light of experience. That is the birth.
commentary: Murugan was born as six infants in a bed of reeds fed by the Ganga. The Ganga is compassion, the soul's own nature. The reeds are forbearance, which bends and never raises the head of ego. Where compassion and forbearance meet, discernment is born. Here, in his early years, is the ground of all Vallalar's later teaching: compassion is the soul's nature, and true knowledge is born from it.

sections.title: The Milk of the Karttikai Mothers

tamil: பின் கார்த்திகை அரிவை பால் கொடுத்த தென்பதென்ன? விவேக விளக்கந் தோன்றுங்கால், பெண்பாலின் குணமாகிய சமனையென்னும் சத்தியின் விளக்கத்தால் இன்பமாகிய அமுத கிரணம் விவேகத்திற்கு ஊட்டுவதே பால் கொடுத்தல்.
translation: What is meant by the Karttikai women then giving him milk? When the light of discernment arises, the ray of nectar, which is bliss, is fed to discernment by the shining of the power (sakti) called Samana, the quality of the feminine. That is the giving of milk.
commentary: The six Karttikai women, the stars of the Pleiades, nursed the six infants. Their milk is the nectar of bliss, given to newborn discernment by the power called Samana, one of the stages beyond Nada in the soul's ascent. Discernment, once born, is fed by inner bliss.

tamil: சுவாமி அம்மையிடத்தில் குழந்தையைக் கொடுக்க, அம்மை குழந்தை ஆறையும் ஒன்றாய்ச் சேர்த்துக் கையால் தடவ, முகம் ஆறும் ஒன்றி வேறாயும், உடல் ஒன்றாயும், கால் இரண்டாயும் ஆனதென்ன? பரமாத்மாவாகிய சுவாமி அரு ளென்னுஞ் சத்தியுடன், தயவென்னும் நதிக்கரையில், சகிப்பென்னும் நாணற்காட்டில், சமாதி முதலிய காலத்தில்? தோன்றி விளங்கும்போது, சுத்த வாசனா தோற்றமாகிய அறுபொறியாகிய குழந்தையை யருள் வசமாக்க, அருட்சத்தி விகாரமன்றி அவிகாரமாய் அறு பொறியையும் அருட்போதக் கையால் அடக்க, விஷயங்களை அறிந்து தோயாமலிருக்க அறுபொறிகள் ஒன்றாயும், குறிஆறாயும், அனுபவவிளக்கம் சாதனவிளக்கம் இரண்டுந் திருவடியாயுந் தோன்றி, சமாதிநிலை விளங்குவதே.
translation: The Lord gave the child to the Mother. The Mother gathered all six children into one and stroked them with her hand, and the six faces became one yet distinct, the body one, and the feet two. What is this? The Lord, the Supreme Self, appears and shines with the Power called Grace, on the bank of the river called compassion, in the reed forest called forbearance, at the time of samadhi and the like [?]. Then, to bring under Grace the child, the six senses, which are the appearing of pure latent impressions (vāsanā), the Power of Grace, without change and unmoved, subdues all six senses with the hand of Grace-awareness. So that they know objects without being steeped in them, the six senses become one, the marks stay six, and the two, the shining of experience and the shining of practice, appear as the holy feet. That is the shining forth of the state of samadhi.
commentary: The Mother, Siva's consort, took the six infants in her arms, and they became one child with six faces, one body and two feet. Inwardly: when the Lord shines with Grace in samadhi, Grace takes the six senses in its hand and stills them. They then know objects without being soaked in them. The senses become one, their marks stay six, and the two feet are experience and practice. The editors marked "at the time of samadhi and the like" with a query [?]: the printed text is uncertain there.

tamil: பிண்டத்தில் இவ்வண்ணமாக இருக்க, அண்டத்தில் இவற்றிற்கு ஊர், ஆலயம், மூர்த்தி, செய்கை முதலியன உண்டாவானேன்? ஆன்மாக்கள் புண்ணிய பாவ கருமங்களால் பேதப்பட்டு, மந்தம் மந்ததரம் ராஜசம் தாமசம் கருமம் முதலிய வேறுபாடுகளால் அனாதி தொடங்கி இன்றளவில் - உயிர்த்திரள் ஒன்றானாலும் - கரணக் கூட்டுறவால் வெவ்வேறு தன்மையாய் விளங்குகின்றன. ஆதலால் மாகருணையுடைய கிருபாநிதியாகிய சிவபெருமான் திருவருளை அங்கையிற் கனியெனவுணர்ந்த அனாதி நித்திய முத்த சித்தராகிய ஈசுவரதத்துவ புவனானுபவ ஈசுவரனால், நாம் உய்யும்பொருட்டு உலகத்தின்கண், பாசநூல்(1) பசுநூல்(2) பதிநூல்(3) அனுபவநூல்(4) என்னும் புராண(1) வேத(2) ஆகம(3) உபநிஷத்துக்கள்(4) உண்டு பண்ணப்பட்டிருக்கின்றன. அவற்றின் வாயிலாகக் கர்மகாண்டம், பத்திகாண்டம், உபாசனா காண்டம், தந்திரகலை, மந்திரகலை, உபதேசகலை முதலிய பேதங்களும், இவற்றிற்கு முக்கியமான ஆசாரம், வருணம், ஆசிரமம் முதலியவைகளும், இவற்றிற்கு ஏதுவான சரியாதி நான்கும், இவற்றிற்கு அடைவாகிய சாலோகாதி நான்கும், இவற்றிற்கு மார்க்கமாகிய தத்துவம், புவனம், பதம், வர்னம், மந்திரம், கலை முதலியனவும் நிர்ணயித்து, பாவநாசத்திற்கு ஏதுவான அனசன சாந்திராயண முதலிய பிராயச் சித்தங்களை விதித்து, இவைகள் செய்வதற்கு யோக்கியமான நதி முதலியவற்றையும், அவற்றிற்கு அங்கமான - தத்துவானுபவங்களாகிய உண்மை நாமங்கள் கெடாதிருக்க - திருப்பெயர் முதலியவைகளை மூர்த்தி ஸ்தல முதலியவைகளுக்கு ஏற்படுத்தி வழங்கச் செய்தார்கள்.
translation: Since this is so within the body, why do they have towns, temples, images, rites and the like in the world outside? Souls are divided by deeds of merit and sin. From beginningless time to this day, through such differences as dull, duller, rajasa, tamasa and karma, they appear with different natures through their union with the inner faculties, though the multitude of lives is one. Therefore Isvara, who experiences the world of the Isvara tattva, a Siddha eternal and free from beginningless time, who knew the holy Grace of Siva Peruman, the treasury of mercy full of great compassion, as plainly as a fruit in the palm of the hand, brought into being in the world, for our uplift, the scripture of bondage (the Puranas), the scripture of the soul (the Vedas), the scripture of the Lord (the Agamas) and the scripture of experience (the Upanishads). Through them He set out the divisions: the section of rites (karma kāṇḍa), the section of devotion (bhakti kāṇḍa), the section of worship (upāsana kāṇḍa), the art of tantra, the art of mantra, the art of instruction, and the rest. He set out what is chief for these: the rules of conduct (ācāram), caste (varṇam), the stages of life (āśramam) and the like; the four beginning with chariyai (service), which lead to these; the four beginning with sālōkam (dwelling in God's world), which are their attainment; and the paths to them: tattvas, worlds, states, letters, mantras, kalas and the like. He prescribed expiations such as fasting and the chāndrāyaṇa (a fast that grows and shrinks with the moon) for the destruction of sin, and rivers and the like fit for performing them. As limbs of these, so that the true names, which are experiences of the tattvas, should not be lost, He gave holy names and the like to images, shrines and the like, and put them into use.
commentary: If all this is within, why outer shrines, images and rites? Because souls, one in essence, differ by their deeds and their natures. The text names four scriptures and pairs each with a stage of the soul: the Puranas for bondage, the Vedas for the soul, the Agamas for the Lord, the Upanishads for experience. With them came the forms of worship, conduct, expiation and pilgrimage, and outer names given to keep the inner names from being lost. Caste (varṇam) and the stages of life (āśramam) appear here among what the scriptures set down. In his later teaching Vallalar declared caste, the religions and their rules false.

sections.title: Holy Days, Kavadi, Six Letters and Temple

tamil: உபாசிக்கின்றவர்களுக்குத் தத்துவநாமங் கெடாமல் அருட்சத்தி தோன்றக் கிருத்திகையையும், வேதாந்த விளக்கத்திற்கு விசாகத்தையும், சதா சுபத்தைக் குறிக்கச் செவ்வாயையும், ஆறு குறியைக் குறிக்கச் சஷ்டியையும், ஞான நிறைவைக் குறிக்கத் தைப் பூசத்தையும் சுட்டினார்கள். தத்துவங்களைக் கையிலெடுத்து ஆடுவதான போத மெனுங் கையால் விஷய பலத்தைத் தத்துவமாகிய காவடியில் கட்டித் தானாகிய தோளிலேற்றித் தான் கெட்டுத் தான் அவனாகிப் போதவடிவனாய், சங்கல்ப தீவிரனாய், சுப்பிரமணிய தத்துவமாய் விளங்கும் திருவுருவ முன்னுக்கு விஷயாபாவ நியாயமே காவடி யெடுத்ததாயும், சுத்த வைராக்கிய நிச்சய சிவபோதமே இடும்பனாயும் குறிக்கப்பட்டிருக்கின்றன. இருதயாகாச ஷட்கோண வடிவமே யந்திரமாய், அதன் அங்க வேறுபாடே நாற்பத்து முக்கோணமாய், உபாங்கமே நவகண்டமாய், உண்மையே சகரமாய், விஷய நீக்கமே ரகரமாய், நித்திய திருப்தியே வகரமாய், நிர்விஷயமே ணகரமாய், பாவ நீக்க ஏதுவே பகரமாய், ஆன்ம இயற்கைக்குணமே வகரமாய் விளங்குவதே ஆறெழுத்து. நமது சரீர இருதய ஸ்தானமே கோயிலாய், மாயாவிசித்திரமே மயிலாய், நாபியந்தமே பலிபீடமாய், உண்ணாவின் மேலந்தமே கொடி மரமாய், பஞ்சகோசங்களே பிராகாரமாய், முக்குணங்களே வில்வமரமாய், ஆன்ம தயையே தடாகமாய், வாயே வாசலாய், அனுபவ நிலையே கோபுரமாய் விதிக்கப்பட்டிருக்கின்றன.
translation: For those who worship, they marked out the star Krittikai, so that the Power of Grace might appear without the names of the tattvas being lost; the star Visakam for the shining of Vedanta; Tuesday to signify constant good; the sixth lunar day (shashti) to signify the six marks; and Thai Poosam to signify the fullness of wisdom. With the hand called awareness, which takes up the tattvas and plays with them, one ties the weight of objects to the kavadi, which is the tattva, and lifts it onto the shoulder, which is oneself; the self perishes, the self becomes Him. Before the holy form that shines as the form of awareness, intense in resolve, the Subramaniya tattva, the principle that objects are absent is what is meant by carrying the kavadi; and the certain Siva-awareness of pure dispassion is what is meant by Idumban. The six-pointed form of the space of the heart is the yantra (sacred diagram); its division into limbs is the forty-three triangles; its lesser limb, the nine sections. Truth as the letter sa, removal of objects as ra, eternal contentment as va, freedom from objects as ṇa, the cause of the removal of sin as pa, the natural quality of the soul as va: this shining is the Six Letters. The heart-place of our body is ordained as the temple; the wonder of maya as the peacock; the end of the navel as the altar of offering; the upper end of the uvula as the flagstaff; the five sheaths as the enclosing walls; the three gunas as the bilva tree; the soul's compassion as the temple tank; the mouth as the entrance; and the state of experience as the tower.
commentary: Each outward sign keeps an inner name alive. The holy days of Murugan are each given a meaning. The kavadi, the decorated pole devotees carry on their shoulders to his shrines, is the weight of the senses' objects, carried until the self is lost in Him: it stands for the absence of objects. Idumban, who first carried two hills on such a pole, is the certain awareness of pure dispassion. The six letters Sa-ra-va-ṇa-bha-va ("born in the reed pool"; the Tamil writes bha as pa) each name a quality, from truth to the soul's own nature. Last, the temple is the body: the heart its shrine, the mouth its gate, the soul's compassion its sacred tank.

tamil: ஞானிகள் கடவுளை எங்கும் உபாசிப்பார்கள் என்றும், யோகிகள் இருதயத்தில் உபாசிப்பார்கள் என்றும், கர்ம காண்டிகள் அக்கினியில் உபாசிப்பார்கள் என்றும், பத்தி காண்டிகள் விக்கிரகத்தில் உபாசிப்பார்கள்* என்றும் விதித்திருக்கிறது. அதற்கு ஒத்தவண்ணம் தத்துவ விசாரத்தையே ஆலயமாக்கினார்கள். ஆலயத்தில் விளங்கும் மூர்த்தியின்பால், பாசங்களில் செல்லும் ஆத்மாக்களை சிவபாசத்தில் பாசநூலைக்கொண்டு அழுத்தி, பசு நூலைக் கொண்டு(?) மேற்குறித்த தந்திர மந்திர கலைகளைக் குருமூலமாய் உபதேசகலையால் விளக்கி, காண்டத் திரயத்தால் நிலைக்கப்பண்ணி, பதிநூலால் அறிவைவிளக்கி, அனுபவநூலால் சமாதியைத் தெரிவித்திருக்கிறது. இவற்றைச் சீவர்கள் மறவாதிருக்க மானைக் காட்டி மானைப் பிடிப்பது போல், ஆலயத்தில் மூர்த்தியாகிய சண்முகப்பெருமானைத் தத்துவவுருவமென்று விளக்கிக் காட்ட, அர்ச்சக வுருவமான ஆசாரியன், நமது அறிவாகிய கர்ப்பூரத்தில், சுப்பிரமணிய உண்மையாகிய விளக்க மென்னும் பிரகாசத்தைக் கொண்டு, அசுத்த விஷய முதலிய எண்ணங்கள் நம்முடைய பொறிகட்குப் புலப்படாமலிருக்க, உண்மை நாதக்குறியாகிய மணி யொலியுடனே தரிசிப்பிக்கச் செய்தும்; வேறு பராக்கன்றித் ததாகாரமாய் நிற்க, நமது தரத்திற்கொத்த உபசாரதியர்களால் வழிபடச் செய்தும் - தத்பல மடைய உத்தமர்கட்கு அன்னவினியோகம் செய்வது மார்க்கமென்று சித்தாந்தம் பண்ணினார்கள்.
translation: It is laid down that the wise (jñānis) worship God everywhere, the yogis in the heart, those of the section of rites in fire, and those of the section of devotion in images (see the editor's note). In keeping with this, they made the inquiry into the tattvas itself the temple. Toward the image that shines in the temple, the souls that go after bonds are pressed into the bond of Siva by the scripture of bondage (the Puranas); by the scripture of the soul (the Vedas) [?] the arts of tantra and mantra named above are made clear through the guru, by the art of instruction; they are made firm by the three sections; knowledge is lit by the scripture of the Lord (the Agamas); and samadhi is made known by the scripture of experience (the Upanishads). So that living beings should not forget these, as a deer is caught by showing a deer, the image in the temple, Shanmukha Peruman, is shown clearly as the form of the tattvas. For this the teacher (ācārya), in the form of the priest, brings to the camphor, which is our knowledge, the flame called shining, which is the truth of Subramaniya. So that thoughts of impure objects and the like do not reach our senses, he gives us sight of the Lord with the sound of the bell, the sign of true Nada. So that we stand absorbed in that form, with no other distraction, he has us worship with the services suited to our level. And they settled as doctrine that, to gain the fruit of this, giving food to the worthy is the path.
commentary: The four ways of worship are those of the old texts (the editor's note gives the classical source): the wise worship everywhere, yogis in the heart, ritualists in fire, devotees in images. The temple is inquiry into the tattvas made visible, and each of the four scriptures has its part in leading souls from bondage to samadhi. As a decoy deer draws a deer, the image draws the seeker inward: the camphor is our knowledge lit by the truth of Subramaniya, the bell is Nada. The editors marked "by the scripture of the soul" with a query [?]: the printed text is uncertain there. The passage names feeding as the path. In Vallalar's later teaching, feeding the hungry became the first work of compassion.

tamil: (பதிப்பாசிரியர் அடிக்குறிப்பு: ஊன்கணார்க்குப் படிமையினும், அந்தணர்க்கு வேள்வித்தீயினும், யோகிகட்கு உள்ளத்தினும், ஞானிகட்கு எவ்விடத்தும் வெளிப்படுதலால். - பரிபாடல் 2-65, பரிமேலழகர் உரை.)
translation: (Editor's note: "Because He appears in the image to those with eyes of flesh, in the sacrificial fire to the Vedic priests, in the heart to the yogis, and everywhere to the wise." Paripadal 2.65, commentary of Parimelazhagar.)

tamil: இவ்வண்ணமாய், அனாதி தொட்டு இன்றுவரை சென்ற நாட்களிலுள்ள அருணகிரியார் குமரகுருபரர் நக்கீரர் முதலிய மகான்கள் தொண்டு செய்து, உத்தம ஞானிகளாய் நித்திய முத்தர்களாய் விளங்குகின்றார்கள். ஆதலால் நாம் யாவரும் அவ்வுண்மைக் கடவுளை வேதாகம விதிப்படி உண்மையாய்ப் பத்தி செய்து அவர் அருளைப் பெறவேண்டும்.
translation: In this way, from beginningless time to this day, great souls of days gone by such as Arunagiriyar, Kumaraguruparar and Nakkeerar did service, and they shine as the highest of the wise, ever free. Therefore all of us must worship that true God truly, with devotion, according to the rule of the Vedas and Agamas, and receive His Grace.
commentary: Arunagirinathar, Kumaraguruparar and Nakkeerar are among the great poets of Murugan; Nakkeerar's Tirumurugarruppadai is the oldest poem on the six shrines. The closing call to worship by the rule of the Vedas and Agamas is the voice of Vallalar's Saiva years; the introduction to Part Two gives his later teaching. What the work itself has shown throughout stays: the true God is found within, as discernment, compassion and Grace.

tamil: திருச்சிற்றம்பலம்
translation: Thiru Chitrambalam.

tamil: சுப்பிரமணியம் முற்றிற்று
translation: Here ends Subramaniyam.

The Vast Grace Light; God in Vallalar's later teaching.
"The light of grace": the name by which his followers called Vallalar.
A target as large as a mountain, which cannot be missed.
The mantra that gives the deity a seat (āsana) and invokes it into its form (mūrti).
A classical Tamil work on daily conduct; verse 4 is quoted.
Salutation to the weapon mantra (astra), held to drive off what hinders.
The weapon mantra ending in phaṭ, a syllable held to drive away what hinders; said while ringing the bell.
Bauhinia racemosa.

glossary.term: Ātma-tattvāya svadhā, Vidyā-tattvāya svadhā, Śiva-tattvāya svadhā
glossary.tamil: ஆத்மதத்துவாய சுவதா, வித்யாதத்துவாய சுவதா, சிவதத்துவாய சுவதா
glossary.def: The tattva mantra of the sips: an offering to the soul tattvas, the knowledge tattvas and the Siva tattvas. Svadhā is a word spoken with an offering.
Encircling (editor's gloss).
Knowing; "the hand of awareness".
Renown.
Nada, the shining of the soul; also the gem between the brows.
Betel leaf with areca nut, chewed after meals.
Betel leaf, areca nut and lime chewed together as a digestive.
Bael tree, sacred to Siva. Bael (Aegle marmelos).
Here the inner light that, with the sound of Nada, can hold the seeker at the outer door.
The small world of the body and the great world of the universe.

glossary.term: bound mind, pure mind, inner mind, gathered mind
glossary.def: The four kinds of mind, the four faces.
To prostrate or bow in salutation.
A cloth burnt whole, which keeps its shape but can no longer serve; the image of the freed one's body.
Fried and sweet preparations such as vadai, adhirasam, dosai, modakam.
A caste name, the caste the old order held lowest of all; kept as a name, not translated.
Telling tales that set people against each other.
Service, worship, yoga and wisdom.
The Tuesday Fast; viratha a vow kept with fasting and restraint, murai its order.
The fibre left after chewing betel; spat out.
The Hall of Consciousness; also within, the seat of the soul between the brows.

glossary.term: cleansing the body, cleaning the teeth
glossary.def: The morning cleansing before the bath.
Ficus racemosa.
Fullness without envy; also envy (மாச்சரியம்) itself, held down in the Lord's hand.
A medicated salve drawn along the eyelid.
The perfect open Space of pure true knowledge, in which God shines.
Kindness that feels for another; Grace is God's compassion, Jeevakarunyam the compassion of living beings.
The soul's natural quality; the Ganga, the lotus, the temple tank.
A way of living held to steadily; four kinds in this work.
Holding the mind on the Chit Sabhai, with restraint of fault-finding, pride, anger and lust.
Standing towards all people as one's own self, with no distinction of caste, religion or any other kind.
Guarding the organs of knowledge and turning the organs of action to service.
Compassion for the souls of all 8,400,000 kinds of birth; seeing the soul as the Hall and its inner light as the Lord.
Areca nut boiled and dried.
The daily rite of the Anushtana Vidhi, completed before this worship.
Siva as the silent teacher, facing south.
Sight: going to see Siva in the temple and the Guru.
The reddening of the sky before sunrise.
Going along with others out of politeness or obligation.
Murugan's consort at his left; the tattva of restraint (தாந்தர தத்துவம்).
The old threefold desire.
A servant of Siva's feet: a Saiva devotee.
The cow gesture: the fingers shown like the teats of a cow (editor's gloss); held to turn water into nectar.
Snapping the fingers in all eight directions (editor's gloss).
The power of digestion, which sets the measure of food.
Initiation; this rite is for one who has received Saiva initiation.
The knowledge that distinguishes the true from the false.

glossary.term: distinctions of attainment of a slight fraction of the Suddha Sanmarkkam experience
glossary.def: His verdict on the sects and paths such as Vedanta and Siddhanta.

glossary.term: distinctions of attainment within the tattvas
glossary.def: His verdict on the religions with their practices, gods and goals.
A cloth put on the image to dab away the water after the bath.
Dūrvā grass with unbroken rice (akṣata), the offering proper to Ganapathi.
Amorphophallus paeoniifolius; the word also means compassion.
Medically induced vomiting.

glossary.term: Erakam, Tiruvavinankudi, Pazhamudircholai, Tiruchendur (Tirucheeralaivai, Tiruchendil, Jayantipuram), Tirupparankundram, Kunruthoradal
glossary.tamil: ஏரகம், திருவாவினன்குடி, பழமுதிர்ச்சோலை, திருச்சீரலைவாய், திருச்செந்தில், செயந்திபுரம், திருப்பரங்குன்றம், குன்றுதோறாடல்
glossary.def: The six shrines.
Eternally liberated.
Wrong conduct, the opposite of the true path.
Atonement prescribed by the elders (Skt. prāyaścitta).
Penance for sin; a fast that grows and shrinks with the moon.
Five fragrant spices added to betel, usually cardamom, clove, nutmeg, mace and edible camphor.
Arising, growing, removal of fault, bewilderment, clearing; mirroring the five divine acts.
The five coverings of the soul; the temple walls.
Mixed rice dishes such as sweet pongal, curd rice, tamarind rice.

glossary.term: food unfit to eat and contrary to the Vedas
glossary.def: Food forbidden by the scriptures, above all flesh.
Bending without raising the head of ego; the reeds.
Lakshmi, goddess of wealth and fortune.
The elephant-faced god, remembered first.
The elephant-faced god, worshipped first as remover of obstacles.
The Worship of Ganapathi; pūjā worship with offerings, vidhi rule.
Sandal paste and the other offerings (கந்தம், sandal paste, fragrance).
The second part, periodic care and restraint for everyone.
God.
Adultery; as a sin of the mind, thinking of it.
The golden hall of the dance of grace.
A priestly lineage by which a family names itself.
God's Grace, here the flame that lights the soul's awareness.
God's Grace and its working power.
Siva, in the Saiva idiom.
One in whom goodness itself shines; the elders who prescribe expiation.
Realised souls, whom the weak and aged may serve.
The three qualities, rajas, tamas and sattva; here in their pure state.

glossary.term: half or three-quarters of a meal
glossary.def: Half or three-quarters of a normal meal.
The hall God had built at Vadalur; today the Sathya Gnana Sabai.
Injury to others (Skt. hiṃsā).
Hṛdayāya namaḥ, the first of the six limb mantras, used to touch the places of the body.
Vallalar's name for karisalanganni and thuthuvalai.
The service the great one commands, done without a break.
One living a family life.
Songs and words in praise of God.
The one who first carried two hills on a pole to Murugan.

glossary.term: imagined lore of attainments within the tattvas
glossary.def: His verdict on the Vedas, Agamas, Sastras and Puranas.
Things the mind has made up.
Setting to work.
Latent tendencies (Skt. vāsanā) of body, senses and inner faculties. Traces left in the mind by past experience.
The lowest grade of impurity.
The offering and waving of incense and lamps.
Mind, intellect and the other inner instruments.
The inner faculty of knowledge, which inquires and decides; here "the tattva that is our soul's knowing".
The mind held on the single act of relieving the body.
Pure tattvas of Saiva teaching; levels of knowledge and action.
A watch of three hours (seven and a half nāḻikai).
Repetition of a sacred name.
Compassion for all living beings, the foundation of spiritual life in Vallalar's teaching. Here ஜீவர்களிடத்தே காருணியம், "compassion towards living beings".
One freed while still living.
Body of wisdom.
Garland of kadamba flowers; the rejection of all the tattvas.
Kadamba tree (Neolamarckia cadamba).
Chebulic myrobalan (Terminalia chebula).
The five kalās, Nivritti, Pratishtha, Vidya, Santi and Santyatita: the five spheres into which Saiva teaching divides the worlds.
The mantra said with the sandal paste; meaning uncertain (see notes).
A coarse rice of the monsoon season; avoided.
False daisy (Eclipta prostrata), a Siddha "herb of wisdom".
The sections of rites, devotion and worship.
The six stars of the Pleiades who nursed the six infants.
Ebony (Diospyros); some identify it with black cutch (Senegalia catechu).
Salutation to the armour mantra (kavaca), held to enclose and protect.
A decorated pole carried on the shoulders to Murugan's shrines.
Ironwood (Memecylon umbellatum).
The forms of life; traditionally 8,400,000 (எண்பத்து நான்கு நூறாயிரம்).
What the freed one's form, senses, mind and experience become.
Here the genital sac; elsewhere a sheath of the soul.
Pillow (editor's note: தலையணை).
Holy days of Murugan.
The worship of the water pot whose water serves the rite.
White teak (Gmelina arborea).
Hiptage (Hiptage benghalensis), a flowering climber.
A thick gravy and a thin peppery broth.
Weeping or complaining in vain; reading uncertain (see notes).
The image of the unwavering mind.
The two aspects of each of the six centres; the twelve hands.
Shell lime spread on the betel leaf; நீறு also means sacred ash.
Compassion.

Done in the mind: worship performed inwardly.
Arjuna (Terminalia arjuna).
Emetic nut (Randia dumetorum).

The three doors through which merit and sin come, four kinds each.
The root centre at the base of the trunk.
Root nature, the primal matter of the tattvas; the peacock.
A thorny wild nightshade (Solanum); identification uncertain.
Premna, a shrub whose leaves are cooked as greens.
Mukia maderaspatana, a medicinal creeper.
Murugan as worshipped at Vaitheeswaran Koil.
The subtle inner sound.
A channel of the vital breath in the body.
Food offered to the deity; sāmānya (ordinary) and viśeṣa (special).

A unit of 24 minutes; 60 make a day and a night.
"Salutation", "I bow": the closing word of each mantra; the print writes nama.
Indian sarsaparilla (Hemidesmus indicus).
Medicine put into or drawn through the nose.
Siva as the dancer in the hall of Chidambaram.
Jamun, Java plum (Syzygium cumini).
Prickly chaff-flower (Achyranthes aspera).
Murugan's companions; the nine tattvas of dispassion.
Freedom from desire, desirelessness.
Looking (editor's gloss).
The south-west quarter, named after its regent Nirriti.
Rules of Daily Conduct; nithya daily, karma duty, vidhi rule.
A Saiva poem on daily observance.
Five-leaved chaste tree (Vitex negundo).
A thing set apart as dedicated to Vaidyalingar.
Salutation to Siva as the sun.
Salutation to Vaidyanatha, the Lord of healers.
The first part, the householder's day.
Speech, hands, feet and the organs of excretion and generation.
Ears, skin, eyes, tongue and nose.
Literally "camp"; Murugan's six great shrines; here places where the soul rests in stillness.
A Siddha work on the properties of foods, plants and habits.
A meal of fruit (editor's note: பழ ஆகாரம், பழ உணவு).
A traditional weight, about 35 g.
The sheath of a palm's flower cluster.
The five-syllable mantra of Siva (Na-ma-si-vā-ya); the Omkara Panchakshara (ஓங்கார பஞ்சாக்ஷரம்) adds Om.
Literally pollen or powder; here a weapon meaning the removal of bondage. Reading unclear.
The supreme teacher.
Reading aloud of sacred texts. Recitation of a scripture.
A classical Tamil anthology; its medieval commentator.
Attachment, desire (see notes).
Leaves offered in worship.
The body made of the elements.
The pedestal on which the image stands.
Rice cooked soft; here of raw (unparboiled) rice (பச்சரிசி).
Alternanthera sessilis (sessile joyweed), a green valued for the eyes.
Circumambulation, walking round the deity with it on one's right.
Maya as primal matter, the source of the bodily tattvas.
The sacred syllable Om.
Body of the primal sound Om.
The power that governs a tattva.
Sprinkling (editor's gloss).
A shrub, probably white berry bush (Flueggea); identification uncertain.
Indian sorrel (Oxalis corniculata).
Pongam (Millettia pinnata).
Discernment free of objects, in which all six faculties of knowing meet; the Subramaniya tattva.
A medically induced purge.
A medically induced purge.
A Siddha method of preparing a herb by steeping or boiling it in milk.
The aims of human life; here the four great fruits of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
The three he names together; their customs are not to be observed, nor held as true.
One who has renounced the world.
Remorse that sees the wrong and turns from it.
Rice milled without parboiling.
The ignorance at the root of bondage.

glossary.term: rules of conduct, caste, stages of life
glossary.def: Set down by the scriptures in this text; Vallalar later declared caste false.
The hall of God's presence; here the soul itself.
Ash worn on the forehead and body in Saiva practice.
The ceremonial bathing of the image.
Holy people.
Two states of the soul: joined to body and instruments, and lying alone in darkness.
The four attainments: dwelling in God's world, nearness, likeness of form, union.
Absorption of the mind in God.
A power, one of the stages beyond Nada in the ascent of yoga.
Universal harmony; first word of the name Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam.
Pure goodness, the natural quality.

glossary.term: scriptures of bondage, the soul, the Lord, experience
glossary.def: The Puranas, Vedas, Agamas and Upanishads.
Going to see Siva in the temple.
Heart-leaved moonseed (Tinospora cordifolia).
A small-grained fragrant rice of Tamil Nadu.
The organs of sense.
A measure of about 280 ml (the Madras seer).
The six ends: Yoganta, Kalanta, Nadanta, Bodhanta, Vedanta and Siddhanta, the summits of six schools, held in harmony by the path.
"The Six-Faced", a name of Murugan.
A perfected being; here "ever free, pure, and of the body of wisdom".
The all-powerful perfected form God takes in Vallalar's body.
Saiva Siddhanta, the doctrine that the Lord, the soul and bondage are beginningless and eternal; also "settled doctrine".
Attainment; here of action, of yoga and of wisdom (கருமசித்தி, யோகசித்தி, ஞானசித்தி).
The house at Mettukuppam, near Vadalur, where Vallalar lived in his last years.
Wrong deeds and their fruit: pleasant at first, painful in the end.
God as named in the Saiva idiom of his earlier years; "the thought of Siva" (சிவசிந்தனை), "meditation on Siva" (சிவத்தியானம்).
The Saiva scriptures of temple and daily rite.
Salutation to Siva's Ganapathi, the god worshipped first as remover of obstacles.
Salutation to the Guru who is Siva: the initiating teacher, honoured as Siva.
The experience of Siva.
Salutation to Siva as the sun.
Salutation to Siva: the Panchakshara.
The knowing of the five senses and of the soul.
Murugan's six-letter mantra, "born in the reed pool".

glossary.def: Tattvas, worlds, states, letters, mantras, kalas.
One-sixteenth; eighth part (அரைக்கால்): one-eighth.
A floor smeared clean, traditionally with a cow-dung wash.
Backbiting.
Murugan's chief weapon: power, grace and knowledge. Babul (Vachellia nilotica).
The third part, the stricter day of one who gives the whole day to the path.
Giving food at one's own cost.
The knowledge that is dispassion.
Rest, peace; a play on ஆறு, six.
The sacred stories of Siva.
Murugan, son of Siva.
Murugan, the God with six faces (Skt. Subrahmaṇya); in this work, the soul's pure knowledge beyond all tattvas.
Pure body; also called the golden body.
The pure true path; "the true common path of all religions, all sects and all paths".
Slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), the edible lime paste used with betel and in preparing dry ginger. Strongly alkaline: used neat or in excess it burns the mouth, throat and eyes.
The demon Murugan defeats; the great ahankara.
Here the ritual code a family follows, named with its gotra.
Tapping (editor's gloss).
Tapping three times (editor's gloss).
The salutation to Ganapathi: tapping both temples lightly with the knuckles.
An offering of water with a mantra.
The constituent principles (plural tattvas) of which bodies, senses, minds and worlds are made.
The mantra of the three tattvas, said with the three sips: Ātma-tattvāya svadhā, Vidyā-tattvāya svadhā, Śiva-tattvāya svadhā (see the Anushtana Vidhi).
Derived from the tattvas; "the tattvas and tattvic things" (தத்துவ தாத்விகங்கள்) make up the body.
The goddess of Vaitheeswaran Koil, consort of Vaidyanathar.
The Unique Great Compassion.
The experience by which the body no longer dies.

Bringing into being (தோற்றுவித்தல்), sustaining (வாழ்வித்தல்), removing fault (குற்றம் நீக்குவித்தல்), bringing to ripeness (பக்குவம் வருவித்தல்) and illumining (விளக்கஞ் செய்வித்தல்): God's great acts of compassion.

Salutations to Siva's five faces: Īśāna-mūrdhāya (Isana, the head), Tatpuruṣa-vaktrāya (Tatpurusha, the face), Aghora-hṛdayāya (Aghora, the heart), Vāmadeva-guhyāya (Vamadeva, the hidden part), Sadyojāta-mūrtaye (Sadyojata, the body).

glossary.term: the great life of true and perfect happiness
glossary.def: The same imperishable life.

glossary.term: the great life that is the attainment of supreme bliss
glossary.def: The deathless life, hindered at no time, in no place and in no way.
God, seen as the light within the soul.
The three eternal realities of Saiva Siddhanta.
The twelve places of the body touched with a mantra (see the Anushtana Vidhi).

glossary.tamil: ஹிருதய சிர சிகை கவச நேத்திர அஸ்திர மந்திரங்கள்
glossary.def: Salutations to the heart (Hṛdayāya), the head (Śirase), the tuft of hair (Śikhāyai), the armour (Kavacāya), the eyes (Netrebhyo) and the weapon (Astrāya).
Sixteen names of Ganapathi, from Sumukha (of the pleasing face) to Śivātmaja (son of Siva), each with namaḥ.
Mind, speech and body.
The two sides of the chin, the nostrils, eyes, ears and shoulders (two each), the navel and the chest.
Jñānis, those of wisdom.
Tamil Saiva hymns of the Thirumurai.

glossary.term: Thevaram, Thiruvasagam, Thiruvisaippa, Thiruppallandu, Periya Puranam
glossary.tamil: தேவாரம், திருவாசகம், திருவிசைப்பா, திருப்பல்லாண்டு, பெரிய புராணம்
glossary.def: Tamil Saiva scriptures of the Thirumurai: hymns, and the lives of the Saiva saints.

Vishnu; in the verses, a figure for great wealth.
The True Word of Grace; thiru holy, arul grace, mey true, mozhi word.
Haste.
Keen awareness.
Solanum trilobatum, a thorny climbing nightshade; leaves and berries used.
The pot of holy water for the bath.
The fourth state, beyond waking, dream and deep sleep; its kinds: supreme, pure, guru, Siva, Sakti turiya (பர, சுத்த, குரு, சிவ, சத்தி துரியம்).
The state beyond the mind, the last stage of the yogic ascent (Unmana in the series glossary).
Names of Vadalur (Parvatipuram), north of Chidambaram.
Siris (Albizia); the "great" kind is not certainly identified.
Siva as the healer, the Lord of Vaitheeswaran Koil.
"The bountiful one": Ramalinga Adigal.
Indian pennywort (Centella asiatica).
Murugan's consort at his right, born of a deer among hunters; the pure mind.
A weight of about 4 grams.
Followers of Vedanta.
The scriptures of his hearers: the Vedas and the Saiva Agamas.
What a medicine is taken with.
Ash worn on the forehead and body in Saiva practice.
Strength of the bodily constituents.
One of the six centres; here placed at the heart.
The breath as the carrier of life.
The breath as the carrier of life; to be spent sparingly.
Medically induced vomiting.
White-flowered butterfly pea (Clitoria ternatea), a purgative.
Sacred ash (vibhuti).
Physic nut (Jatropha curcas).
The three humours of Siddha medicine.
The Vedantin's claim to be the pure witness, untouched by action.
The blanket spread on the floor for the night.
A sacred diagram; also "mechanism" in the body.
The yellow-flowered kind (Wedelia / Sphagneticola).
